name: Endicott Pear Tree

location.address: North Shore Medical Center, 100 Endicott Street, Danvers, Massachusetts

access: Free. Stands behind a fence beside a hospital parking lot; viewed from the 2011 historic marker at the viewing level over the lot and from the medical centre's public lobby display. Not enterable.
transport: Danvers, roughly 35 to 45 minutes by car from central Boston; by public transport commuter rail to Salem or Beverly plus a local bus or taxi, 75 minutes or more (not route-checked).
verify_notes:
- Oldest living cultivated fruit tree in North America per enwiki; planted 1632 to about 1640 by John Endecott (spelled Endicott on the tree), governor of Massachusetts Bay Colony. Only survivor of his orchard.
- Alive: search result dates a May 2025 photograph, and a Dec 2024 article says it still bears fruit. I did not open those pages; treat as one soft dated source.
- 1770 storm survived; 1964 vandals hacksawed the branches and trunk down to about 6 ft; chain-link and barbed wire fence then installed. 1952 CBS-Hytron plant and parking lot left it nearly hidden. 2009 lobby display, 2011 marker by Colonial Dames. Reported 80 ft by 1875 (not today). Fruit is a Bon Chretien sugar pear.
- Owner 2004: North Shore Medical Center; maintained with Danvers Tree and Grounds.
- Pin: Wikidata 42.548238,-70.930013 and OSM node 2510773452 (42.548227,-70.930052) agree, but probably share a source and the tree is tucked beside a lot, so left approximate.
- Commons photo is a 1997 USDA photo, public domain: old, check it still shows the tree as it is.
